units.title: One harmonic extension has zero flux at every internal radius
units.reader_note: Real closed-ball specialization for the two zero-flux uses in the source mean-value proof.
units.statement: One harmonic extension agreeing with u on the parent closed ball has integrable zero radial gradient flux for every positive subradius, including the parent radius.
units.formula: \exists v:\quad v=u\text{ on }\overline B(a,R),\quad v\text{ harmonic near }\overline B(a,R),\quad\forall\,0<r\le R,\quad\int_{S^{n-1}}\langle\nabla v(a+r\zeta),\zeta\rangle\,d\tau=0.
assumptions: \(n\ge2\), \(R>0\), \(u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\); source standing dimension and positive parent radius are retained literally.
There exists an actual function \(v\), harmonic in a neighborhood of every point of \(\overline B(a,R)\), agreeing with \(u\) on the whole closed ball.
The same extension is chosen before all subradii. Derivatives are taken of it. The original total \(u\) may be arbitrary and discontinuous outside the ball. Radial L1 is a conclusion.

notation.text: One actual extension, the literal unnormalized polar unit-sphere measure, and any0<r<=R.

steps.title: Retain one actual extension
steps.text: Choose the extension supplied by closed-set harmonicity once. Restrict its neighborhood harmonicity to each smaller closed ball. Equality with the original function remains on the parent ball; no derivatives of the original off-ball representative are used.
steps.formula: v=u\text{ on }\overline B(a,R),\qquad 0<r\le R\Longrightarrow v\text{ harmonic near }\overline B(a,r).
steps.lean: harmonic_closedBall_zero_flux chooses v before introducing r and uses HarmonicOnNhd.mono.

steps.title: Identify actual gradient regularity and divergence
steps.text: Local C2 of the extension gives local C1 of its actual gradient through the Riesz map. In the Euclidean coordinate orthonormal basis, differentiating the actual gradient-component identity identifies its coordinate divergence with the actual Laplacian, which vanishes by harmonicity.
steps.formula: \nabla v\in C^1\text{ locally},\qquad\operatorname{div}(\nabla v)=\sum_i D_iD_i v=\Delta v=0.
steps.lean: gradient_c1 composes fderiv_right with the inverse Riesz equivalence. divergence_gradient differentiates the full component identity and evaluates the actual second Fréchet derivative in EuclideanSpace.basisFun.

steps.title: Apply ball flux and cancel the positive radius factor
steps.text: Apply the canonical ball-flux theorem to the extension gradient on each selected closed ball. It supplies actual scalar radial integrability. The volume integrand is zero; the positive radius power is nonzero, so the radial flux is zero. The same v supplies both the outer and inner source-use candidates.
steps.lean: The public proof calls ball_flux_eq_integral_divergence exactly once per r, retains its L1 conclusion, proves the volume integral zero and cancels the nonzero real radius power.

units.lean_statement: Exact sealed existential-extension statement, with one witness outside the universal quantifier over positive subradii.
